questions.q: A model has an MAE of 10,000 on house prices in dollars. What does that mean?
options: Predictions are off by about $10,000 on average, in absolute terms
The model explains 10,000 units of variance
Ten percent of predictions are wrong
The model is off by exactly $10,000 for every house
questions.explain: MAE is the average absolute error in the target's own units, so 10,000 means about $10,000 off on average. Individual errors can be larger or smaller.

questions.q: In the lesson, one prediction was changed to be off by $150,000. Which metric reacted most strongly, rising from 10,000 to 67,676?
options: MAE
MAPE
RMSE
The intercept
questions.explain: RMSE squares errors before averaging, so one large miss dominates it. MAE rose only to 38,000 for the same change.

questions.q: What does an R-squared of 0 on a test set mean?
options: The model is perfect
The model predicts no better than always guessing the mean
The features are uncorrelated with each other
The test set is empty
questions.explain: R-squared compares the model to always predicting the mean. Zero means no improvement over that baseline, and negative values mean worse than the baseline.

questions.q: When is MAPE a poor choice?
options: When errors are measured in dollars
When you want an easy-to-explain percentage
When the model is linear
When actual values can be close to zero, because the percentage error blows up
questions.explain: MAPE divides each error by the actual value, so near-zero actuals produce huge or undefined percentages. It is best when the target stays well above zero.

questions.q: A straight-line model has R-squared 0.968, but its residual plot shows a clear U shape. What should you conclude?
options: The model is fine because R-squared is high
The residuals are random, so nothing is wrong
The data contain no signal
The relationship is curved, so add a squared term or use a more flexible model
questions.explain: Randomly scattered residuals suggest an adequate fit. A systematic U shape means the model is missing a curve in the data, even if the single score looks good.
